title: Prompt Composition and Generation
description: Assemble system instructions, retrieved context, and user input into safe, effective prompts in C#.

blocks.text: Prompt composition is the step where retrieval, user intent, and system rules meet. In C# backends, compose prompts with clear structure, bounded context, and safety constraints. A weak composer can undo strong retrieval.

blocks.title: Recommended structure
items: System instructions with behavior rules, safety constraints, and output format.
Tool schema if the model should call functions.
Retrieved context with citations and metadata.
Conversation history trimmed to fit the context window.

blocks.text: Retrieved documents can contain text intended to manipulate the model. Treat retrieved content as untrusted and use system instructions to constrain behavior. Do not blindly concatenate retrieved text into the prompt.

blocks.title: Conceptual prompt composer
blocks.content: Use a typed builder to keep prompt composition maintainable.

blocks.title: Guard retrieved text
blocks.text: If retrieved text includes instructions that conflict with your system prompt, the model may follow the retrieved text. Use strong system instructions and consider output filtering.

items.text: I can list the sections of a safe production prompt
items.hint: System instructions, tools, retrieved context with citations, history, user message

items.text: I understand why retrieved text can be unsafe
items.hint: It can contain prompt injection attempts meant to override system behavior

items.text: I can implement a reusable prompt composer in C#
items.hint: Use typed builders or templates instead of string concatenation everywhere

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: Prompt composition is a core backend responsibility.
Structure prompts to separate rules, context, and user input.
Treat retrieved content as untrusted and add guardrails.
blocks.takeaway: Build prompt composition as a first-class service in your backend, not an afterthought in the controller.
